Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 103, verses 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-ʿAsr (The Declining Day/Time), because it opens with God's oath by al-ʿAsr, which is time (al-dahr) and the wonders it contains.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• To affirm and emphasize that mankind is in loss and ruin, except those who are characterized by what saves them: faith and righteous deeds, and mutual enjoining of truth and mutual enjoining of patience. Within this is an exhortation to the deeds that bring about happiness, and an indication of the ruin of those who are heedless of them.

[The Tafsir]

God swore by time (al-dahr), because of the wonders of God's power it contains, which point to His greatness, that humankind is indeed in ruin and loss. It is not permissible for a servant to swear except by God, for swearing by other than God is shirk.
